extracted.intended_audience: broadcasters, broadcast counsel, and members of the public interested in commenting on FCC rulemakings (specifically parties to MB Docket No. 23-287 / RM-11961)
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Communications Commission Notice of Proposed Rulemaking proposing substitution of a TV channel allotment in Idaho Falls and providing procedural instructions for filing comments, technical justification, and the proposed regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be filed on or before October 5, 2023 and reply comments on or before October 20, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public comments are time-limited; see the DATES section. The page also notes 'Comments are no longer being accepted' after the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to filing comments with the FCC, interested parties should serve counsel for the Petitioner at the provided name and address (Patrick Cross, Esq., Brooks, Pierce, McLendon, Humphrey & Leonard, L.L.P., Wells Fargo Capitol Center, Suite 1700, Raleigh, NC 27601).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing comments to this docket, both official filing with the FCC and service on the petitioner's counsel are expected; the document lists the agency filing address (Federal Communications Commission, Office of the Secretary, 45 L Street NE, Washington, DC 20554).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper filing procedures (reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: See Sections 1.415 and 1.420 of the Commission's rules for information regarding the proper filing procedures for comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM directs readers to the cited rule sections for detailed procedural requirements (methods of filing, formats, docketing procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte contact prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: All ex parte contacts are prohibited from the time a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking is issued to the time the matter is no longer subject to Commission consideration or court review (see 47 CFR 1.1208).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are exceptions to the prohibition which can be found in Section 1.1204(a) of the Commission's rules; parties should consult those rules before communicating with Commission staff about the pending proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition justification — public interest standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Petitioner must demonstrate the proposed channel substitution would serve the public interest, here by resolving reception issues experienced by a meaningful cross-section of viewers and expanding availability of reliable free over-the-air network television service within the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM uses the Petitioner's statement that the substitution resolves reception issues as the core public interest justification; factual support (complaints, service area analysis) is used to substantiate this claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technical analysis and de minimis service loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner relied on the Commission's TVStudy software tool to predict service loss from the proposed channel change and reported a predicted loss of only 327 persons, which it characterizes as de minimis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM notes that the TVStudy prediction may not capture ongoing reception challenges under the current facility; petitioners should include technical studies (e.g., TVStudy outputs) and explain limitations or contextual factors when characterizing predicted losses as de minimis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical rationale — VHF vs UHF propagation factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission recognizes that VHF channels pose challenges for providing digital television service: VHF propagation characteristics allow undesired signals and noise to be receivable at relatively farther distances; nearby electrical devices tend to emit noise that can cause interference; and VHF reception often requires physically larger antennas relative to UHF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These technical factors are presented as part of the factual and engineering rationale supporting a move from a VHF channel (channel 8) to a UHF channel (channel 18); petitioners should address such propagation and reception characteristics when justifying channel substitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed regulatory text / table amendment format
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes amending 47 CFR part 73, specifically §73.622 (Digital television table of allotments), to revise the entry for Idaho Falls under Idaho to read: 'Idaho Falls — 18, 20, 36.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM includes the precise amendment language and table-format entry that would be incorporated into the CFR if adopted; submissions altering allotments should provide exact proposed regulatory text and conform to the formatting conventions used in §73.622.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To request materials in accessible formats (braille, large print, computer diskettes, or audio recordings), contact FCC504@fcc.gov or call the Consumer & Government Affairs Bureau at (202) 418-0530 (VOICE), (202) 418-0432 (TTY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document provides specific contact points and lists examples of accessible formats; requesters should use the provided email or phone numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection and regulatory flexibility determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: This document does not contain information collection requirements subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 and does not contain any proposed information collection burden for small business concerns; provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act do not apply to this proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM explicitly states that PRA and RFA analyses are not required for this action; parties should note whether a given proposal contains information collection requirements or regulatory flexibility implications when preparing comments.
